# Errors

Why a pattern was refused, and where in it.

<h2 id="regex-error-kind"><code>RegexErrorKind</code></h2>

```rux
pub enum RegexErrorKind: uint8 {
    UnclosedGroup = 1,
    UnopenedGroup = 2,
    UnclosedClass = 3,
    InvalidEscape = 4,
    NothingToRepeat = 5,
    InvalidRange = 6,
    InvalidCount = 7,
    UnknownProperty = 8,
    UnknownFlag = 9,
    InvalidGroupName = 10,
    DuplicateGroupName = 11,
    Unsupported = 12,
    InvalidText = 13,
    TooLarge = 14,
    OutOfMemory = 15
}
```

What went wrong. `Copy`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Regex/Src/Error.rux#L5)

**Cases**

| Name                 | Value | Description                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `UnclosedGroup`      | `1`   | A `(` has no `)`.                                                                                                                 |
| `UnopenedGroup`      | `2`   | A `)` has no `(`.                                                                                                                 |
| `UnclosedClass`      | `3`   | A `[` has no `]`.                                                                                                                 |
| `InvalidEscape`      | `4`   | A `\` is followed by something that is not an escape, or ends the pattern.                                                        |
| `NothingToRepeat`    | `5`   | A `*`, `+`, `?` or `{n,m}` has nothing before it to repeat.                                                                       |
| `InvalidRange`       | `6`   | A class range ends before it starts, as `z-a` does, or one end of it is a class such as `\d`.                                     |
| `InvalidCount`       | `7`   | A repetition count is over 1000, or its maximum is below its minimum.                                                             |
| `UnknownProperty`    | `8`   | A `\p{...}` names a property or category this package does not know.                                                              |
| `UnknownFlag`        | `9`   | A `(?...)` holds a flag other than `i`, `m`, `s` and `x`.                                                                         |
| `InvalidGroupName`   | `10`  | A group name is empty, or holds something other than letters, digits and `_`, or starts with a digit.                             |
| `DuplicateGroupName` | `11`  | Two groups have the same name.                                                                                                    |
| `Unsupported`        | `12`  | The pattern uses lookaround, a backreference or something else that cannot be matched in linear time.                             |
| `InvalidText`        | `13`  | The pattern is not UTF-8 text.                                                                                                    |
| `TooLarge`           | `14`  | The compiled pattern would be too large, usually from counted repetitions inside each other, or its groups are nested too deeply. |
| `OutOfMemory`        | `15`  | The allocator could not supply the storage.                                                                                       |

<h2 id="regex-error"><code>RegexError</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct RegexError {
    pub kind: RegexErrorKind;
    pub offset: uint;
}
```

Why a pattern could not be compiled, and where. `Copy`.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Regex/Src/Error.rux#L41)

**Fields**

| Name     | Type             | Description                                                                                                              |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `kind`   | `RegexErrorKind` | What went wrong.                                                                                                         |
| `offset` | `uint`           | The byte offset in the pattern where it went wrong; zero for failures that have no place, such as running out of memory. |
